description: Hades carries Persephone off. Her mother Demeter, goddess of the harvest, lets the earth starve. A myth built to explain the seasons.

hero.hook: When a daughter vanishes underground, her mother stops the harvest. The world discovers winter.

blocks.text: **Demeter** was the Greek goddess of harvests and fertility. Her daughter **Persephone** stood for spring. Their story explains the [[agricultural cycle in Greek religion]]: why the earth dies in winter and comes back in summer.

It is also a drama between a mother and a daughter, stretched across the world of the living and the world of the dead. Out of this story grew the [[Eleusinian Mysteries]], secret rites that promised initiates hope in the face of death.

Persephone was first called **Kore**, “the girl”. One day, in a meadow, she picked a narcissus. The ground opened. **Hades**, king of the underworld, burst out on his chariot. With the secret agreement of **Zeus**, her own father, he carried her down to the land of the dead to make her his queen.

blocks.caption: The abduction of Persephone, spring vanishing underground

blocks.text: According to the myth, **Gaia**, the Earth, had grown that narcissus on Zeus's orders. Its scent was meant to trap Persephone.
Demeter, inconsolable, left Olympus. She forbade the earth to sprout. The fields stayed barren. A **famine** threatened humans, and with them the sacrifices offered to the gods. Zeus had to act.

Zeus sent **Hermes**, messenger of the gods, to demand Persephone's return. Hades pretended to obey. Before she left, he offered her a few **pomegranate seeds**. Anyone who eats in the kingdom of the dead belongs to it. The trap was set.

A compromise was needed. Persephone would spend part of the year with Hades and the rest with her mother. When she came back up, Demeter turned nature green again: that is spring and summer. When she went back down, the goddess of harvests withdrew her favor: that is autumn and winter.

blocks.text: Some versions say Persephone did not eat those seeds by accident. Curiosity, or a growing attachment: the story also becomes an entry into adulthood.

While wandering, Demeter stopped at **Eleusis**, near Athens, disguised as an old woman. Taken in by the royal family, she finally revealed that she was a goddess and ordered a temple built. That was the birth of the [[Eleusinian Mysteries]].

Initiates walked for nine days, fasted, and drank the **kykeon**, a brew of barley and mint. In the [[Telesterion]], a vast initiation hall, light burst out after the darkness. Sacred objects were shown there, under total secrecy.
Some modern scholars think the kykeon contained rye ergot, a hallucinogenic fungus. That would explain the visions initiates described.

The rite copied the journey of the goddess. Passing through the death of nature with Demeter, then coming back with Persephone: the participants believed they were winning a better fate in the afterlife.

sections.title: At Eleusis, hope after the darkness

blocks.text: For the Greeks, a grain of wheat buried in the soil lived the same fate as Persephone. It vanished underground and came back as a stalk. The myth ties farming, death, and rebirth together.

It also speaks about ancient marriage, often lived as a painful departure: a girl left her mother to join another household. Between Hades and Demeter, the final deal holds opposites together: shadow and light, death and life.
The time **Persephone** spends in the underworld sets the seasons: her absence brings the mourning of **Demeter** (autumn and winter), her return brings the plants back to life (spring and summer).
